archetypes.name: cutover-fidelity
archetypes.rationale: Large sh-to-py migration with 20+ deleted bash helpers; every shell consumer callsite must be updated correctly, and Makefile target names appear inconsistent between PHONY declarations and shard references.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review whether every shell consumer of the deleted bash helpers (design-publish.sh, design-pause-save.sh, design-pause-load.sh, plan-review-loop.sh, scout-plan-archetypes-wrapper.sh, design-route.sh, list-issues.sh, launch-claude-subprocess.sh, revise-plan-with-waterfall.sh, aggregate-findings.sh, check-recovery-paths-in-plan-scope.sh, tracking-issue-write.sh) has been updated to call the Python CLI with the correct argument syntax, including --title=VALUE quoting for leading-hyphen titles. Verify that the Makefile PHONY declarations are consistent with the actual target rule names and shard references — specifically whether test-check-main-sync vs test-check-main-sync-strip-body and test-record-plan-review-round-timing vs test-record-plan-review-round-timing-strip-body are declared, defined, and referenced consistently. Check that agent-lint.toml exclude entries for deleted files have no dangling comments that reference removed entries. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: assert-defensive
archetypes.rationale: The new named_block_write function uses assert statements for invariants that should produce typed errors, and duplicates classification work in the replace path, introducing silent failure risk.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine python/issue_wire.py named_block_write: the replace path calls strip_named_block then calls _classify_named_block_lines a second time, relying on two bare assert statements (assert span.start is not None; assert span.end is not None) to guard indexing. These asserts can be silently disabled in optimised Python (-O), and the surrounding code path cannot reach them unless the first classification succeeded, making the invariant non-obvious. Flag whether these should be replaced with explicit ShipError or ValueError paths consistent with the malformed-return contract. Also check whether the double call to parse_named_block at lines 1158–1163 vs 1163–1164 constitutes needless redundant gh-free work or whether the second call is load-bearing for the markers_present boolean. Finally, verify that _resolve_issue_wire_repo's except ShipError clause can actually be triggered by gh.resolve_repo_gh_only given its current return-None-on-failure contract. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: kv-routing-contracts
archetypes.rationale: The migration introduces two distinct output channels (emit_kv via fd-3 quiet mode vs raw print to stdout) for different CLI verbs, and the issue_edit_body_with_retry helper must not re-redact already-redacted content; these contract boundaries need independent verification.
archetypes.prompt_body: Verify that python/issue_wire.py correctly separates the two output channels: KV-producing CLIs (plan_block_read_main, plan_block_write_main, named_block_write_main) must route output through logging_util.emit_kv so quiet-mode parents see KVs on stdout while verbosity goes to fd 3, whereas raw-output CLIs (issue_title_eligibility_main, issue_title_archival_jq_main, issue_insert_signal_marker_main, untrusted_*) must print directly to stdout and must not call quiet_init. Check that plan_block_strip_body_main only calls quiet_init on the malformed path (not the success path), matching the plan's raw-stdout-filter contract. Verify that gh.issue_edit_body_with_retry in python/gh.py writes the already-redacted body directly via --body-file without routing through _body_file_args or _fail_closed_redacted, satisfying the no-second-redaction contract; and that named_block_write passes the redacted body to this helper rather than to the general issue_edit path. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
